# ui::FrameColor

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

A color for a part of the system-drawn window frame. It holds one of four answers, where [`std::optional<Color>`](../core/color.md) could hold only two:

[follow()](#follow) - no opinion, the default. In [ChromeHints](chrome-hints.md) it leaves the system's color. In [ChromeOverrides](chrome-overrides.md) it uses the theme's. [system_default()](#system_default) - the system's own color, even over a theme that sets one. [none()](#none) - draw nothing. Windows 11 and the border only. A caption color of [none()](#none) is treated as [system_default()](#system_default). a [Color](../core/color.md) - that color. The conversion is implicit, so `chrome.caption_color = palette.selection` works.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::ChromeOverrides chrome;
chrome.caption_color      = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFF1E1E1E); // a custom color
chrome.caption_text_color = ui::FrameColor::system_default(); // the OS's, over the theme's
chrome.border_color       = ui::FrameColor::none();           // no border line (Windows 11)
window.set_chrome(chrome);
```

## FrameColor

```cpp
constexpr FrameColor() = default
```

[follow()](#follow): no opinion.

## FrameColor

```cpp
constexpr FrameColor(Color color)
```

A custom color; implicit so a plain [Color](../core/color.md) can be assigned.

## kind

```cpp
FrameColorKind kind() const
```

Which answer this holds.

## has_value

```cpp
bool has_value() const
```

True only for a custom color, the one case where `*` means anything.

## operator*

```cpp
const Color& operator*() const
```

The custom color; meaningful only when [has_value()](#has_value).

## reset

```cpp
void reset()
```

Back to [follow()](#follow).

## follow

```cpp
static FrameColor follow()
```

No opinion: [ChromeHints](chrome-hints.md) leaves the OS default, [ChromeOverrides](chrome-overrides.md) uses the theme's.

## system_default

```cpp
static FrameColor system_default()
```

Forces the OS's own color, even over a theme that sets one.

## none

```cpp
static FrameColor none()
```

Draws nothing. Windows 11 and the border only; a caption of [none()](#none) acts as [system_default()](#system_default).
